messages:
jess_support: hey team — a customer in NL reports large spikes and auth 401s starting ~09:10 CET. they say some requests go to us-east instead of eu-west and then fail with 401. i collected a couple reproductions and dig outputs.

leo_ops: ouch. do we have a concrete traceroute/dig?

jess_support: yes. i ran dig +short against two resolvers (customer ISP resolver and 1.1.1.1) from my laptop in amsterdam. same client network but different resolver results. copy/paste below.

jess_support: ```
# to ISP resolver (returns old us-east edge)
$ dig +short @resolver.isp.example api.redwood.example 
34.201.45.12

# to public resolver (returns expected eu-west)
$ dig +short @1.1.1.1 api.redwood.example 
18.194.23.110
```

marta_sre: that looks like partial propagation / ISP cache returning an older A record. TTL for that record? did we recently rotate IPs or failover?

jess_support: TTL shows 300 but i also saw some responses with 60. i suspect upstream resolver is ignoring TTL or has sticky cache. customer said they saw ~200ms extra and then 401s for a while.

alex_eng: were there any rollout changes last night? we pushed a small routing tweak to GeoIP DB 04:30 UTC that switched a subset of EU prefixes to eu-west 2. maybe s3 object not fully replicated.

marta_sre: checking S3 object versions and Cloudflare geodb. give me a sec.

dnsbot: INCIDENT BOT: DNS config changed 2026-03-15T04:30:12Z by alex_eng. GeoIP DB version v2026-03-15.

marta_sre: confirmed: geoip-db v2026-03-15 uploaded to s3://redwood-geo/ but one edge region reported a 503 during propagation window. replication retried and succeeded, but ISPs could have pulled partial data.

leo_ops: that explains some resolvers returning previous edge IPs. but why the 401s? should be same origin.

alex_eng: we have per-region token binding for some auth keys — requests hitting us-east are validated against us-east keys. If a client expects eu-west key and hits us-east, tokens reject -> 401. usually our routing fallback rewrites auth, but not for this legacy token flow.

jess_support: customer paste of failing curl:

jess_support: ```
$ curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-cust-xxxxx" https://api.redwood.example/v1/engines/list
< HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
< x-edge-region: us-east-1
```

marta_sre: ok. plan: 1) confirm geoip db healthy across edges 2) confirm TTLs and set advisory to support for TTL bumps 3) issue guidance to customers to flush local caches if needed and capture dig +trace outputs 4) consider short-term mitigation to accept tokens from fallback regions for 30m.

leo_ops: i'll open a hotfix to accept cross-region token checks for legacy keys (30m window) and coordinate with security for audit trail.

alex_eng: restarting the geo-sync job to force reconcile now. also kicking a targeted cache purge on Cloudflare for domains matching api.redwood.example.

jess_support: customer can you run these three commands and paste results?
1) dig +trace api.redwood.example
2) dig +short @resolver.isp.example api.redwood.example
3) curl -I https://api.redwood.example/v1/ping

customer reply (via email forwarded): ran the three commands. dig +trace shows some hops resolving to us-east for the ISP resolver, 1.1.1.1 shows eu-west. curl ping returns 200 when routed to eu-west, 401 when to us-east.

marta_sre: we have a clear repro. next steps: - escalate to partnerships (ISP outreach) to ask them to clear resolver cache (they're known to follow long cache heuristics) - roll forward a small rollback to ensure both regions accept tokens - publish a short KB for support customers explaining how ISP-level caches can cause this and mitigation steps.

leo_ops: tagging @security for the temporary token acceptance. @security pls ack.

alex_eng: actioned: geo-sync restart started at 2153010000. cloudflare purge started. hotfix PR opened: https://git.internal/r/redwood/edge/+/1234

dnsbot: DEPLOY BOT: Purge started for api.redwood.example — 1200 keys queued.

jess_support: thanks. customer is on standby to test. will update thread with their verification.

-- ~20 minutes later --

jess_support: customer confirms after purge + geo-sync they now consistently get eu-west IP and auth fixed. they still saw a couple of sticky ISP cache hits but they're decreasing.

marta_sre: leaving follow-up: create alert when geo-db upload has partial replication error (503) and add runbook step to immediately trigger CDN purge and notify support.

leo_ops: documented runbook change in https://confluence.internal/redwood/dns-geoip-propagation-runbook

jess_support: closing loop with customer and sending KB. thanks all :thumbsup:
